_doc: Terms the translation keeps fixed. `keep` stays as written in every language; `translations` imposes a word per language; `tone` is the register of each language.

coworker.tr: coworker (suffixes after an apostrophe: coworker'ınız, coworker'lar)

credit.de: Guthaben (a balance), Credit / Credits (a count: "500 Credits")
credit.ar: رصيد (a balance), رصيد / أرصدة (a count: "500 رصيد")

tone.fr: Vouvoiement. Short, plain product French as in a SaaS app. No anglicisms beyond the glossary.
tone.es: Tuteo (tú), as Spanish-language SaaS products do. Neutral Spanish, no regionalisms.
tone.pt: Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR), você, as Brazilian SaaS products write. Never European Portuguese spelling or vocabulary.
tone.de: Duzen (du), as recent German SaaS products do. Short, plain product German; nouns capitalized. No anglicisms beyond the glossary.
tone.tr: Siz, as Turkish SaaS products write. Short, plain product Turkish; a foreign product name takes its suffix after an apostrophe (Slack'e). Never glue a case suffix onto an ICU argument ({name}'e): rephrase so the argument stands alone. No anglicisms beyond the glossary.
tone.ar: Modern Standard Arabic, as Arabic SaaS products write: short, plain, polite. Address the reader in the masculine singular as apps do; buttons use the imperative (احفظ) or the verbal noun (حفظ) consistently. Arabic punctuation (، ؛ ؟). Product and app names stay in Latin script. Digits are Latin (0-9). Plurals: give zero, one, two, few, many and other.
tone.zh: Simplified Chinese as written in mainland China SaaS products: short and plain. Address the reader as 您. Full-width punctuation (，。：？！、). Never the Chinese dash ——, nor the em dash. Product and app names stay in Latin script. Plurals: only `other` is needed.
tone.he: Modern Hebrew as Israeli SaaS products write: short and plain. Buttons and actions in the infinitive (לשמור), sentences addressed in the masculine singular as apps do. Product and app names stay in Latin script. Plurals: give one, two and other.

rules: Never use the em dash (—) nor the en dash as punctuation.
Keep every ICU argument ({name}, {count, plural, ...}) and every rich text tag (<link>...</link>) exactly as in the source.
Translate the words inside plural and select branches, and give every plural category the target language needs.
Stay as short as the English: a button label stays a button label.
